processing_steps_notes.value: Melting and casting in a vacuum-induction melting furnace under 400 mbar Ar pressure. Five Cu molds were moved stepwise inside the furnace and successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.

source.reason: Describes the VIM melting/casting synthesis step of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl RAP set to which the Al-free reference sample belongs.

processing_steps_notes.value: 10×50×130-mm³ blocks hot rolled at 1100 °C into 2±0.1-mm-thick and ~500-mm-long sheets.

source.reason: Hot rolling step applied to the RAP blocks before reheating and cutting.

processing_steps_notes.value: Sheets reheated to 1100 °C, water quenched, and cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments of 2×60×55 mm³ per alloy composition.

source.reason: Reheating + water quenching step applied to the hot-rolled sheets before homogenization.

processing_steps_notes.value: Homogenization at 1100 °C for 2 h under Ar, followed by water quenching. This is the parent process of the 550 °C/1 h aging step.

source.reason: Homogenization step listed in the synthesis route; the sample's process definition lists proc_homog-1100c-2h-wq as parent.

processing_steps_notes.value: Aging conducted in air at 550 °C for 1 h, followed by oil quenching (one of the nine RAP heat treatments at 450/500/550/600 °C for 0/1/24 h).

source.reason: Identifies the 550 °C / 1 h aging condition of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C base material, matching the sample's process definition.

processing_steps_notes.value: Scales removed from the surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.

source.reason: Scale-removal step performed after the heat treatments on the RAP materials.

processing_steps_notes.value: Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation were prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

source.reason: Sample preparation step for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation.

other_conditions.value: Tensile specimens prepared by package spark erosion from 2×60×55 mm³ segments; all plotted values represent averages of three measurements per material state.

source.reason: Figure 3d shows hardness nearly flat around 200 HBW from 0Al to 6Al (the Al-free reference condition included), and b0023 states aging increases hardness slightly.
RAP mechanical screening included room-temperature tensile testing (initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1) and hardness measurements on the Fe-30Mn-1.2C base composition across aging conditions.
Fully recrystallized microstructure retains some microsegregations of Mn.
Grain size of ~20 µm reported for the fully recrystallized microstructure after hot rolling and water quenching.
Single austenite phase prevails at room temperature for Al contents below 5 wt.% (this alloy has 0 wt.% Al).
Bulk microstructure of the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C material: fully recrystallized austenite with ~20 µm grains and retained Mn microsegregations.

The Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy has <5 wt.% Al, so a single austenite phase prevails at room temperature (b0015); hot rolling and water quenching resulted in a fully recrystallized microstructure (b0021).

unmapped_findings: For the Fe-30Mn-1.2C (0 Al) reference alloy, aging leaves the yield strength virtually unchanged and increases the hardness slightly, but reduces UTS and total elongation; embrittlement becomes most apparent for long aging times (24 h) and higher temperatures (>500 °C). This qualitative trend applies to the 550 °C/1 h aged condition, but no specific numeric YS/UTS/TE values are reported for that condition in the text.

The best mechanical behavior for the Al-free ternary Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy was reported for the as-homogenized state (360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS, 77% TE); these values belong to the as-homogenized sample and not to the aged-550°C-1h sample.
The as-cast samples had a coarse dendritic microstructure before hot rolling (pre-hot-rolling initial state).

The RAP screening produced a matrix of 45 different sample conditions (5 Al levels × 9 heat treatments) for the Fe-30Mn-1.2C base composition; the 550 °C/1 h condition is one of these nine heat treatments.
